subject: Manipulate spatial weights matrix in INLA

messages.author: 218ba84dd8032360
messages.subject: Manipulate spatial weights matrix in INLA
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to manipulate a spatial weights matrix in fitting a spatial CAR model in INLA.  In the benchmark model, I specified a conventional spatial weights matrix in which a value of 1 indicates two areas are adjacent to each other, while a value of 0 indicates otherwise.

In the second model, I modified the binary spatial weights matrix used in the benchmark model by weighting each adjacent area by its relative population size.  For example, if a focal area has three adjacent areas whose population sizes are 100, 200, and 300, respectively; then the corresponding spatial weights for each adjacent area are 100/(100+200+300)=1/6, 200/(100+200+300)=2/6, and 300/(100+200+300)=3/6.

However, the parameter estimates from the two models with different spatial weights matrices are identical.  Can someone help me understand what's wrong here?

Thanks,
Hongwei

>
> I am trying to manipulate a spatial weights matrix in fitting a
> spatial CAR model in INLA.  In the benchmark model, I specified a
> conventional spatial weights matrix in which a value of 1 indicates
> two areas are adjacent to each other, while a value of 0 indicates
> otherwise.
>
> In the second model, I modified the binary spatial weights matrix
> used in the benchmark model by weighting each adjacent area by its
> relative population size.  For example, if a focal area has three
> adjacent areas whose population sizes are 100, 200, and 300,
> respectively; then the corresponding spatial weights for each
> adjacent area are 100/(100+200+300)=1/6, 200/(100+200+300)=2/6, and
> 300/(100+200+300)=3/6.

Hi,

if you're using model 'besag' then the argument 'graph' only defines
the graph not the precision matrix (or in your notation, the weights),
itself. they are predefined for that model. 

If you want your own weights, you can use, f.ex, one of the generic
models, do

inla.doc("generic")

to see the documentation.

Best
H


--
